DEFINE
Audio research prototype

Shape the accent. Keep the voice.

Prototype-anchored exemplar conditioning for precise accent control in zero-shot text-to-speech.

About DEFINE

DEFINE takes the voice and the accent as two separate examples: a reference prompt fixes who is speaking, while short exemplar clips of any speaker fix the accent. A single guidance weight w, chosen after training, sets how strongly the accent is applied. The system uses one model and one forward pass, with no accent label and no conversion stage after synthesis.

01Accent transfer

Each row keeps the speaker from the voice prompt and takes the accent from a recording by a different person. Every system receives identical inputs and generates the same unseen sentence.

What to listen for

F5-TTS has no accent control, so it renders the prompt speaker's own accent. The cascade converts the waveform with a separate voice-conversion model, which moves the timbre away from the prompt. DEFINE changes the accent while the voice stays the prompt's.

02Continuous accent strength

The same model and exemplar clips at increasing guidance weight. Nothing is retrained between columns; w is one scalar applied at synthesis time.

Audio is 24 kHz mono WAV. Accent references are drawn from Common Voice; voice prompts come from a licensed voice bank. Samples are generated at w as labelled.
